<reason>A established the decisive distinction between an Egyptian veto and reciprocal, independently enforced safeguards. It directly answered pressure about shortage allocation and deadlock, explaining how interim rules could permit continued operation without Egyptian approval. B’s development case justified building the dam, but not exclusive authority over cross-border drought risks. Its repeated equation of slower filling with shutting down generation overstated the trade-off and misrepresented A’s position.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s pressure question elicited B’s rejection of any compulsory slowdown, even under an independent, reciprocal rule. A then demonstrated that B opposed enforceability itself, not merely Egyptian domination. Its distinction between slowing additional storage and stopping turbines further undermined B’s claimed development-versus-veto dilemma.</best_rebuttal>
